_purpose: Canonical 3D-scene vantages for the visual-regression + perf sweeps (scripts/probe-sweep.js). This is the golden spec: each vantage teleports the probe to a fixed camera + time/sea, captures one screenshot, and records fps. The `expect` text is what a correct frame looks like; `regressions` lists the specific failures this vantage exists to catch (each has bitten a real release). Data-driven per the infinite-of-x rule - add a vantage here, both sweeps pick it up. Coordinates are the same debug/camera_request.json + debug/showcase_request.json fields lib.rs polls.
_perf_note: perf_floor_fps is an advisory lower bound at this vantage on the dev machine (RTX 4070). The perf sweep flags a stop below it; it is a smoke threshold, not a hard gate.
_clock_note: READ THIS BEFORE PICKING A `time`. The showcase `time` field is a GLOBAL clock, not the local solar hour at the vantage (src/engine/ipc.rs:200-205 feeds it straight into the world clock). The local solar hour is roughly `time + lon/15`. So time 12.0 is local noon only near lon 0; at lon 138.8 (the Fuji vantages) time 12.0 is about 21:15 LOCAL and the frame comes back as a night scene. Pick `time = desired_local_hour - lon/15`, wrapped into 0..24. This trap cost `ground-storm-inslab` its whole purpose from v0.1070 to v0.1073: it was installed as the permanent BUG-049 daylight gate and was silently rendering at night, so every cloud LIGHTING change was being judged in the dark.

vantages.expect: Dense green ground with real 3D conifer trees standing around the camera - visible brown trunks, needled canopies - and BAKED SILHOUETTE cards, ragged crown outlines with sky visible through their edges, never plain rectangles, carrying the forest toward the horizon. Grass underfoot - drawn by the instanced strand layer (v0.1090), NOT by patch-baked cards, which were deleted in that increment. This vantage aims within 10 deg of the horizon, so judge the sward on fuji-grass-underfoot instead; here it only has to be present and to end without a visible ring. BACKLIT FOLIAGE GLOWS: crowns seen against the sky read as luminous yellow-green with visible leaf structure, never as black shards. CROWNS ARE OPAQUE MASSES (v0.1088, cluster cards): a crown seen against the sky blocks most of it, and what occludes is FOLIAGE, not branch. Sakura in bloom reads as bare branches SLEEVED in blossom, not a pink haze: the pink mass follows the branch lines. BARK CARRIES SURFACE STRUCTURE AT FOREST RANGE (added for the v0.1089 bark rung). On any trunk whose visible width is >= 24 px and whose vertically-solid interior mean luma is >= 40, the cross-trunk high-pass detail energy (5-tap moving-average residual RMS / run mean; luma = 0.2126R+0.7152G+0.0722B; measured over horizontal runs >= 16 px that are vertically solid bark for +/-20 rows, so twigs inside foliage cannot contaminate it) must be >= 0.030 at 1280x720 and >= 0.040 at 2560x1387, AND the ABSOLUTE residual must exceed 1.5 luma levels. MEASURED v0.1088.2: 0.0103 at mean luma 25.8 here and 0.0048 at mean luma 67.0 on ground-storm-inslab = 0.27 and 0.32 luma levels absolute, against a smooth-ramp 8-bit quantization floor of 0.258 for the same filter, i.e. BOTH vantages measure no bark signal at all at ~4 m. REFERENCE, in-repo CC0 photoscan assets/models/plants/pine_sapling_small/textures/pine_sapling_small_bark_diff_2k.jpg under the identical metric: 0.0503 at 116 px, 0.0367 at 58 px, mean luma 57, whole-image albedo CoV 0.134. Like the backlit-canopy gate this is RESOLUTION DEPENDENT: record capture_w in the manifest and judge only at the width the gate is written for. BARK IS SPECIES-SPECIFIC: crop one trunk of each species in frame and compare - no two species may share a fissure morphology, and sakura in particular must read as SMOOTH bark with horizontal lenticel bands, not vertical plates (Prunus x yedoensis is smooth reddish-grey with 1-3 cm lenticels and NO furrows; Betula is white with peeling papery strips and black lenticel bands; Pinus is orange-red flaking plates; Quercus is deep vertical furrows between ridged plates; palm is a fibrous column of ringed leaf scars, not fissures at all). BARK STRUCTURE IS MULTI-OCTAVE: a radially-averaged 1D power spectrum of the high-passed cross-trunk profile on the nearest trunk must spread energy across at least three octaves with no octave holding more than 60% of the total (a single-octave fissure field concentrates > 85% in one band; the in-repo CC0 scan holds 0.0732 at 2048 px and 0.0755 at 512 px, flat across scale, which is what multi-octave means). BARK HAS A SPECULAR RESPONSE THAT VARIES ACROSS THE SURFACE: on a trunk lit by sun or by a bright overcast sky the 95th-percentile luma of trunk pixels must exceed the median by >= 1.5x, and the bright pixels must form a broken, position-dependent pattern rather than a smooth band along one edge - a constant-roughness cylinder produces the smooth band and cannot produce the break-up (MEASURED v0.1088.2 on the widest storm trunk, 31 px: peak 60.8 against a mean of 58.6, a 4% swing with no separable specular lobe, because the plant branch pins roughness = 0.9 at 90-fragment-main.wgsl:1195 and the bark branch only lerps 0.78..0.96 by one octave, faded by `detail` at :1315; the in-repo CC0 ARM scan reads pine bark roughness 0.69-0.86, mean 0.776).

NO flat rectangular slabs anywhere in the tree field: every card past the 3D-model ring shows a crown outline with sky visible through its edge. 6 of the 8 rows in data/vegetation/trees.ron are procedural (model: "") and had NO atlas tile, so they fell through planet_chunks.rs:1925 to plain coloured trunk+canopy rectangles; fir and pine took the sprite path but a SHIPPED build has no assets/models/ (.github/workflows/build-desktop.yml copies data/ + assets/icons/ + assets/shaders/ only), so the bake aborted, tree_atlas_ready stayed false and their cards painted the flat green fallback at 90-fragment-main.wgsl:824. NO black backlit canopy. In the crop (900,0)-(1700,500) the MEDIAN luminance of canopy pixels must be at least 0.10x the median of sky pixels in the same crop, and fewer than 30% of canopy pixels may fall below luma 16. MEASUREMENT: luma = 0.2126R + 0.7152G + 0.0722B; a pixel is SKY if B > R and B > G (the dome is blue-dominant, foliage never is) and CANOPY otherwise - note that lumps trunks, branches and deep interior gaps in with the leaves, which is why the dark-fraction half of the gate is 30% and not 20%. MEASURED v0.1080.1 (before): ratio 0.026, dark fraction 58.5% (the finding's own slightly different classifier read 0.063 / 53.9% on its capture). MEASURED v0.1081 (after): ratio 0.448, dark fraction 22.8%, same rig, same config, same crop. Cause of the failure: tree_mesh::blade() emitted through PlantMeshBuilder::tri2, which never sets self.organ, so every foliage face on sakura/momiji/oak/birch/acacia (and every blossom) carried Organ::Stem, bit 19 was clear, 90-fragment-main.wgsl:1157 is_leaf was false, and the canopy was shaded by the BARK branch at :1259 with no transmission at all. Palm was the only correct species. The leaf-flutter gate at 00-bindings-vertex.wgsl:682 reads the same bit, so v0.1080 foliage wind had no flutter on any procedural tree either. MEASURED AT 2560x1387, AND THIS GATE IS RESOLUTION DEPENDENT: the residual dark is geometric aliasing of sub-pixel leaf blades (no MSAA - every MultisampleState in src/renderer/pipeline.rs is count 1), so the SAME v0.1081 build measures 0.448 / 22.8% at 2560x1387 and 0.211 / 35.3% at 1280x720. The ratio half passes at both widths; the dark-fraction half passes at 2560 and FAILS at 1280. Judge this only on a 2560-wide capture and record the capture width in the manifest. WHY EVERY CAPTURE BETWEEN v0.1081 AND v0.1095 CAME BACK 1280x720, corrected 2026-08-02: NOT 'a second rig running concurrently', which is what this line used to say. Every launch asks for with_maximized(true), but winit can only apply MAXIMIZED through ShowWindow, and from v0.1081 a background launch is created hidden and shown by launch_focus::show_window_behind with SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE, which never carried the maximize - so a rig window opened at the with_inner_size fallback of 1280x720 while `just play` opened at 2560x1387. It was deterministic, not a race. Fixed v0.1095 by sizing the window to the monitor work area with SWP_NOACTIVATE, and scripts/probe-sweep.js now takes --width (default 2560) and marks any vantage that comes back at another width ok:false. RE-BASELINED 2026-08-02 AT 2560x1387, crop (900,0)-(1700,500), both rigs, settled: v0.1095 dev rig (photoscan fir+pine present) sky median 135.6, canopy median 33.6, ratio 0.248, dark fraction 32.3% - the ratio half passes and the DARK half now FAILS, against 0.448 / 22.8% at v0.1081, so this regressed across the v0.1082-v0.1095 arc and nobody could see it at 1280. CARD/MODEL SIZE MATCH at the handoff: capture the same acacia or palm from just inside and just outside tree_model_distance (120 m). The silhouette height must agree within 10% and the trunk base must sit on the ground in both, with NO vertical hop as the camera crosses the ring. Cards are emitted h x h (planet_chunks.rs:1717 `let w = h;`) while the baker frames a square on max(width, height) and returns a footprint the atlas builder discards as _fp (billboard_bake.rs:167-171 and :103), so a crown WIDER than the tree is tall renders about 27% too short with its trunk base about 13% of the card height off the ground. Acacia is that case by construction (tree_mesh.rs:545, "the crown is WIDER than the tree is tall"); fir and pine are height-dominant, which is why the defect was invisible while only they took the sprite path. This is a MOTION gate - walk the ring, do not just compare two stills.

FIR AND PINE MUST BE VISIBLE IN A SHIPPED BUILD. They are invisible today (audited at v0.1085, from source, all three legs confirmed) at EVERY distance, and THIS RIG CANNOT SEE IT. Judge this only in a --shipped-assets rig that junctions assets/icons and assets/shaders alone. FIX: build a procedural form mesh for every registry row - tree_mesh::build_tree already dispatches purely on def.form (src/renderer/tree_mesh.rs:441-447) and fir/pine already carry form: "conifer" - and fall back to proc:{id}_v{va} when the glTF key is absent.

CROWN GAP FRACTION (v0.1088, cluster cards). On an isolated crown against sky, measure per-column chords (topmost to bottommost non-sky pixel): sky-through-crown must be <= 0.30 and the wood/dark-to-foliage ratio <= 0.35:1. Real behaviour is Beer-Lambert for canopies, gap = exp(-K*LAI/cos(theta)) with K ~= 0.5, so a cherry at LAI 3 transmits 22% and an oak at 4.5 transmits 10%; visible woody area is 10-20% of plant area in a leafed crown. MEASURED v0.1087.1 at 1280x720, box (790,40)-(990,175): gap 32.6%, foliage 30.5%, wood/dark 37.0%, ratio 1.21:1; the whole canopy band (0,0)-(1280,200) read 2.89:1. Root cause: the geometric blade layer alone delivers LAI 0.31-0.50 (sakura 9.9 m2 of leaf, oak 48.4 m2, both derived from the generator itself), i.e. 5-10x short, and closing it with blades would cost ~60,000 triangles per tree against a MAX_TRIS of 8600. RE-BASELINED 2026-08-02 AT 2560x1387 (dev rig, settled, hold_altitude). v0.1095, two boxes on isolated sakura crowns: (1587,256)-(1818,422) gap 24.3%, foliage 45.2%, wood/dark 30.4%, ratio 0.67:1; (1856,250)-(2125,397) gap 29.2%, foliage 50.7%, wood/dark 20.1%, ratio 0.40:1. So at 2560 the GAP half passes and the WOOD half fails by 1.9x and 1.1x - the crowns are not transparent so much as they are visibly more branch than leaf. v0.1096 after the crown-depth change, blossom-only box (1587,282)-(1722,384): gap 25.1%, foliage 59.0%, wood/dark 15.9%, ratio 0.269:1, so BOTH HALVES PASS on a crown-only box for the first time. A box that also contains a bole still reads 0.635:1 ((1280,186)-(1459,371)), which is the measurement's own limitation, not the tree's: frame the CROWN, not the tree. Numbers are dev-rig; the shipped rig has procedural fir and pine in place of the photoscans and reads slightly fuller. CI TWIN (runs without a GPU): renderer::tree_mesh::tests::cluster_cards_reach_target_lai_and_fit_the_budget asserts the card layer delivers the species' target_lai within 25% and still fits MAX_TRIS.

NO FLAT-BOTTOMED CANOPY PLATE (v0.1096). On an isolated crown against sky, vertical foliage extent / silhouette height must be >= 0.40, and the standard deviation of the per-column LOWEST foliage pixel must be >= 0.15x that vertical extent. A plate scores near 0 on the second half. Real forest-grown temperate broadleaves carry a live crown ratio of 0.35-0.60 (forestry management targets >= 0.40 for oak) and an open-grown Prunus x yedoensis 0.7-0.8, because laterals are shed over 1-3 m of stem rather than from one whorl, and that is also why a real crown's lower boundary is a lobed sheath instead of a level cut. MEASURED AT v0.1095 from the generator itself: broadleaf() spawned all three primaries from ONE point (the bole top) and emitted foliage only on generations 2 and 3 of a fixed max_depth of 3, so on an 8 m sakura every foliage-bearing twig end sat between y 6.3 and 6.8 m - live crown ratio 0.25 against a 7 m spread, aspect 3.5:1, a mushroom cap with a straight-cut underside, and every cap in the stand bottoming out at the same world height. FIXED v0.1096: a continuing leader to ~0.85 H sheds 6 laterals at stations spanning the crown zone, length falling with station height and insertion angle rising toward vertical, each lateral taking its own generation count from its own length; foliage is keyed on shoot RADIUS (twice the physical twig radius) rather than on a generation number, because with per-lateral depths a generation number describes nothing physical. MEASURED AFTER, from the CI twin: live crown ratio 0.40-0.62 across all 12 broadleaf variants (sakura 0.40/0.54/0.48, momiji 0.48/0.62/0.50, oak 0.49/0.62/0.54, birch 0.49/0.62/0.49), aspect 1.19-2.51:1, and the lowest twig in each of 8 azimuth sectors spreads 0.14-0.25 of the crown depth where a plate would score 0. CI TWIN: renderer::tree_mesh::tests::crown_depth_is_a_real_live_crown_ratio, which asserts both halves and prints an [lcr] line per variant every run. GOTCHA FOR THE NEXT WRITER: the first cut of this put laterals out at 52-62 deg from vertical and the 2560 capture came back with long BARE ARMS silhouetted against sky, because a lateral's first generation carries no foliage by construction. 44-56 deg tucks that run back inside the neighbouring foliage. Do not widen it again without looking at a capture.

CARD SUN/SHADE SPLIT (v0.1088). Within one crown, the mean luma of the sun-facing third must exceed the away-facing third by >= 1.8x, and no card may render as a uniform flat patch - the SD of luma WITHIN a single card's screen footprint must exceed 6/255. A card lit by its own flat quad normal scores 1.0x and 0: every card with the same facing renders at identical brightness, with hard steps where two cards abut. Cluster cards carry per-corner normals blended 0.70 toward the outward direction from the CLUSTER centre and then 0.30 toward the outward direction from the CROWN centre, so a tuft shades as a ball and the crown as a lit sphere. NOTE the far-field card path does the OPPOSITE on purpose (planet_chunks.rs:1686/:1727 pin card normals to the radial up, the v0.896 black-slab fix), which is why a distant forest reads as a flat green carpet - do not 'fix' the near cards by copying it. CI TWIN: renderer::tree_mesh::tests::card_normals_are_spherified_not_flat.

CROWN AMBIENT GRADIENT AND BACKLIT SATURATION (v0.1088). (1) The mean luma of a crown's top third must exceed its bottom third by >= 1.8x on the SAME crown. (2) The brightest decile of green-dominant canopy pixels must hold saturation (max-min)/max >= 0.45: a backlit leaf is lit mostly by the beam transmitted THROUGH it, chlorophyll transmits selectively in the green, so transmitted light is MORE saturated than the leaf's own reflectance. MEASURED v0.1087.1 at 1280x720: canopy band saturation 0.302, right crown 0.269, against leaf albedo saturation 0.55 (sakura) / 0.62 (oak) in trees.ron, with 0% clipped pixels - so this is full achromatic sky ambient landing on every leaf regardless of depth in the crown, NOT a tonemap problem. Top/bottom-third luma read 1.30/0.92/0.65/0.67 across four boxes, i.e. ~1.4x at best. Fix rides on a per-card baked AO scalar (ao = exp(-k*depth-inside-the-crown-envelope), interior landing at 0.20 of the shell) multiplying the AMBIENT term ONLY, never the sun term - the sun already has the shadow map. RE-BASELINED 2026-08-02 AT 2560x1387 (dev rig, settled). v0.1095, same two crown boxes as the CROWN GAP entry: top/bottom-third luma 38.5/58.5 = 0.66x and 72.7/59.5 = 1.22x, i.e. one crown is BRIGHTER AT THE BOTTOM than the top, against a 1.8x gate; brightest-decile saturation of green-dominant canopy pixels 0.406 and 0.506 against a 0.45 floor, so it splits. v0.1096 after the crown-depth change: gradient 1.57x (blossom-only box) and 1.33x (two-tree box), saturation 0.372 and 0.389. The gradient improved because a deeper crown has somewhere for the interior to BE, but BOTH HALVES STILL FAIL and neither is a geometry problem: the ambient term lands on every card regardless of how deep in the crown it sits (the baked AO scalar multiplies it, but the AO is computed against the crown envelope, which just got bigger), and the saturation number is full achromatic sky ambient washing out chlorophyll transmission. This gate is waiting on the AMBIENT path, not on the generator. CI TWIN: renderer::tree_mesh::tests::cluster_ao_darkens_the_crown_interior.

CANOPY CASTS DAPPLE, NOT RECTANGLES (v0.1088, RESTATED 2026-08-02 - THE OLD FORM OF THIS GATE NOW PASSES FOR THE WRONG REASON AND MUST NOT BE TRUSTED). The old form asked for an 8x8 px tile-mean SD above 6/255 on the forest floor, and it was written at v0.1087.1 when the floor read 1.3-1.9 (a flat carpet, no flecks at all). The v0.1090 instanced grass strand layer then landed, and the floor is now ITS texture, not the canopy's: RE-MEASURED AT 2560x1387 2026-08-02, tile-mean SD 16.18 under canopy and 23.44 in the open at v0.1095, and 14.86 / 27.08 at v0.1096 (FIDELITY measured the same thing at 1280x720 and got 15.2 / 22.6). Every one of those clears 6/255 by 2.5x while the frame contains no sunflecks whatsoever, and the number is HIGHER in the open than under the canopy, which is the exact opposite of what dapple would do. So the statistic is measuring strand contrast. UNTIL IT IS RESTATED THIS GATE IS NOT EVIDENCE OF ANYTHING. What it has to become, one of: (a) the same SD taken with veg_density 0 so the sward is out of the frame and only the canopy's own shadow varies, (b) a sunfleck-specific statistic - the area fraction of connected bright components inside the crown's ground shadow, which is what a sunfleck IS and which strands cannot fake, or (c) the ratio of under-canopy SD to open-ground SD, which must exceed 1 and currently sits at 0.55-0.69. The straight-edge half below is unaffected and still binds. NO shadow boundary in the frame may be a straight line longer than 40 px at a non-terrain angle. A straight-edged shadow means alpha-cutout foliage is stamping its FULL QUAD into the shadow map, i.e. the foliage draw is going through the depth-only shadow pipeline (src/renderer/pipeline.rs:566 and :711, both fragment: None, so there is no alpha test at all) instead of an alpha-testing variant. That would be visibly WORSE than today's no-dapple state and will read as a bug the moment the operator walks under a tree. The shadow ortho box is 1.5 km at ~0.73 m/texel, so a 0.5 m cluster is about one texel: expect soft blobby flecks, not crisp ones.

BLOSSOM MORPHOLOGY AND PLACEMENT (v0.1088). On the nearest sakura, connected components of blossom-coloured pixels must have a median area consistent with a 3-8 cm flower cluster at that distance, not a 1-3 px speck. Prunus x yedoensis: 3.5 cm flowers, five NOTCHED petals, 3-6 per umbel, umbels a few centimetres apart along the twig, opening BEFORE the leaves. Through v0.1087 the blossom was a single 0.090 m pink triangle (2.6x life size, wrong shape) scattered through a 0.74 m ball, so a cherry rendered as a green-and-pink dust cloud. Alpha-tested cluster cards STACK, and unlike triangles that cost scales with RESOLUTION: at 2560x1387 the frame is 3.85x the pixels of the 1280x720 the vegetation A/B set was measured at, so headroom that survives at 720p need not survive there, let alone on the cheap hardware this project targets. Budget the crown as OVERDRAW, not as triangles. The generator reports the expected figure every CI run (LAI / mean sprite coverage): 5.7 alpha-test layers per canopy pixel for sakura at v0.1088, and 5.9 at v0.1096 after the crown-depth change (the LAI fit holds target_lai fixed, so a deeper crown buys its extra volume with more cards, not more layers). MEASURED AT 2560 2026-08-02, first time this was possible (the window-size fix, see the backlit-canopy entry). Dev rig, RTX 4070, settled, hold_altitude, veg_density 0.6 -> 0.1: fuji-forest-ground 36.6 -> 33.3 ms, ground-storm-inslab 39.5 -> 33.3 ms. NEAR/CARD HANDOFF IS INVISIBLE, and tree_card_hide_m must TRACK COVERAGE. Walk from 1 m to 8 m from a single tagged tree: crown silhouette height and width must agree within 8% across the geometry/card switch and no foliage element may pop, appear or vanish at the boundary (a MOTION gate, like the 120 m CARD/MODEL SIZE MATCH entry above). NO OPEN TWIG TIPS: no terminal limb may show a flat elliptical cut face against the sky. PlantMeshBuilder::tube emits no end cap and the v0.1086 weld only plugs junctions where a CHILD buries itself in a parent, so a terminal tip is an open pipe you can look down. Photographed at v0.1087.1 in .probe-rig-opt/crop_crown_raw.png. The cluster-card emitter places a CAP card just beyond every terminal tip, facing along the twig, for exactly this reason.

NO GRASS RING. The baked grass cards were deleted in v0.1090 and replaced by a camera-relative instanced strand layer whose density ramps to zero with DISTANCE (45 tillers/m2 inside 6 m, 14 at 12 m, 0 at 22 m) instead of stepping with patch depth. The old gate was patch depth >= 18, so the field ended wherever the LOD selector happened to stop refining - a hard edge that moved with the camera and lit up at grazing sun (v0.999 operator report: 'a line of light perpendicular to me like 10 meters away'). There must be no circular boundary in the ground cover at any distance, and NOTHING may re-introduce a hide-radius handshake between two grass stages: there is only one stage now. v0.1091: the layer draws here (12,830-12,940 tillers, capture .probe-rig-r2/sweeps/20260801-204553/fuji-forest-ground.png) and this gate has a CI twin - terrain::planet_chunks::tests::grass_harvest_recentring_cannot_change_what_is_drawn - so it is no longer only a visual judgement. See that vantage's HARVEST RECENTRING regression for why a hysteresis-only design cannot pass it.

THE CLUSTER SPRITE BAKE RUNS ONCE PER SESSION, NOT ONCE PER FRAME (v0.1089 commit 1). MECHANICAL CHECK: `[Cluster] N sprites in` must appear EXACTLY ONCE in a session's run.log. MEASURED v0.1088.2: 1671 such lines in a ~1700-frame session in .probe-rig-bark/logs/run.log at 89-123 ms each, and an independent rig counted 1808 lines against ~1260 frames at a median 82 ms. src/lib.rs:9386 calls bake_cluster_sprites(None) unconditionally inside the near-tree block, and that block is guarded only by `chunked_drawn && tree_dist > 1.0 && alt_over < 2500.0` (src/lib.rs:9277) - the `if moved > 12.0` hysteresis closes ABOVE it, and every consumer below is skipped by decoration_mesh_cache.contains_key, so the whole result is thrown away after the first frame. Each call rebuilds a shader module + pipeline (src/renderer/billboard_bake.rs:482), allocates 1024^2 colour + depth targets (:600) and does a blocking device.poll(Maintain::Wait) readback per sprite (:955). ABLATION MEASURED: with the bake removed both this vantage and ground-storm-inslab went from 96.8-103.8 ms to the rig's 33.3 ms vsync ceiling, a saving of at least 65 ms (>= 2.95x), while removing every near-tree DRAW instead moved the frame only 2.4%. The images are bit-identical because the sprites are a pure function of tree_mesh::registry(), so this vantage and ground-storm-inslab must still satisfy their full expect line and EVERY entry in this list unchanged. Keep the dump_dir path uncached: the {"bake":"trees"} showcase PNG dump is a dev aid and must still re-bake on demand.

BARK MUST NOT FADE TO A SMOOTH TUBE WITH DISTANCE. Measure the cross-trunk detail energy on one tagged trunk at 1.5 m, 4 m, 10 m and 30 m: it must not fall below 60% of its 1.5 m value anywhere inside 30 m. Through v0.1088.2 the procedural bark albedo was scaled by detail = 1 - smoothstep(2.5, 12.0, dist) (assets/shaders/pbr/90-fragment-main.wgsl:1205) and the relief by micro = 1 - smoothstep(0.8, 3.0, dist) (:1207), so relief died at 3 m, albedo at 12 m, and the whole branch was skipped past 12 m - while a ground-level forest frame is ~90% stand at 3-40 m. THE SHADER MATHS WAS NEVER THE DEFECT: a bit-faithful CPU replica of hash21/voronoi_edge over the real trunk domain returns 26-41% crack coverage at every trunk radius from 0.02 m to 0.50 m, and the network is plainly visible in a 1.1 m capture (.probe-rig-bark2/closeups/p11.png). The fades existed because a per-pixel procedural has no mip chain; a baked, mipped, anisotropically-filtered texture removes their reason for existing, so the wood branch must carry NO distance gate on albedo, normal, roughness or AO. Do not retune the constants - retuning only moves the aliasing back in.

NO ONE-BARK-FOR-EVERY-TREE. CI TWIN (runs without a GPU): assert the bark bake emits one distinct layer per row of data/vegetation/trees.ron and that no two layers' luma histograms correlate above 0.9 - a shared field with a per-species tint scores ~1.0 and fails. The morphology selector must be a DATA field in trees.ron (infinite-of-X), not a match on species id in Rust. Through v0.1088.2 the bark branch (90-fragment-main.wgsl:1288-1331) took no species input at all: coordinates bp = ((obj_p.x+obj_p.z)*2.4, obj_p.y), literal frequencies 1.6 / 7.0 / 9.0, and eight flat trunk_color tints in trees.ron (fir .075/.055/.038, pine .085/.062/.042, sakura .062/.047/.046, momiji .070/.052/.040, oak .080/.058/.038, birch .52/.50/.46, acacia .10/.078/.050, palm .13/.10/.068), so a cherry, an oak, a birch and a palm carried identical bark.

BARK TEXEL DENSITY IS FIXED IN WORLD SPACE, NOT MODEL SPACE. The baked bark UVs must express a metres-per-tile scale, so a 22 m tree and a 4 m sapling of the same species show the SAME physical fissure size; verify by cropping one species at two very different height_m values and confirming the fissure period in metres agrees within 15%. The v accumulator must be a running ARC LENGTH in metres divided by the tile height, not a per-segment 0..1: trunk() emits tubes with a deliberate joint overshoot (src/renderer/tree_mesh.rs:677, `seg + rb*0.5`) and limb() with `seg_len + rb*0.7` (:1622), so a per-segment v restarts the texture at every one of the ~6 joints on the bole. Precedent for the failure mode: the fir/pine photoscans draw with scale = height_m / TREE_MODEL_H (src/lib.rs:9759, TREE_MODEL_H = [[1.27,0.92,0.70],[1.06,0.85,0.83]], height_m 22.0 and 16.0), i.e. 15.1x to 31.4x, so the one real bark scan in the repo renders at 15-31x life size with roughly 9-16 mm texels. Same defect class as the v0.1086 ten-times-oversized leaves.

@group(3) BINDINGS 11 AND 12 ARE OCCUPIED, NOT FREE. They are undeclared in assets/shaders/pbr/00-bindings-vertex.wgsl (which jumps 10 -> 13) but ARE real entries in the Rust layout: src/renderer/pipeline.rs:321 and :331, the atmosphere transmittance (256x64) and multiple-scattering (32x32) LUTs, bound at all three sites (src/renderer/mod.rs:1123/1127, 1193/1197, 1627/1631). Both are texture_2d<f32> Float{filterable:true}, so a new @binding(11) would TYPE-MATCH, raise NO validation error, and silently sample an atmosphere LUT as bark - worse than a crash. If a future rung genuinely needs a second bark map, take binding 16, never 11 or 12. And after ANY change to that layout, count entries at ALL THREE create_bind_group sites INCLUDING the lazily-built 'Material Albedo Bind Group' at src/renderer/mod.rs:1575 - that is the one missed in v0.1029, and menu-only boots stayed green through ten releases while every world entry panicked. Verify by ENTERING THE WORLD: node scripts/probe-sweep.js --only fuji-forest-ground,ground-storm-inslab, panics must be 0.

BARK AO RIDES THE ALBEDO LUMA, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE TRADE (v0.1089). The shipped bark map is ONE per-species linear RGBA8 = (normal.x, normal.y, luma, roughness) on the EXISTING per-material albedo slot, with hue coming from material.base_color (= trunk_color) - so crevice occlusion is folded into the luma channel rather than carried as a separate ambient-only AO term. CHECK: compare the sunlit third of a trunk against its shaded third - the fissure pattern must be VISIBLE in both and must not DEEPEN on the sunlit side (satisfied by construction here, since a luma multiply scales sun and sky identically). WHAT THIS GIVES UP, on purpose: (a) within-species hue variation such as lichen and moss, and (b) a separately-controllable ambient-only AO of the kind the v0.1088 cluster cards use. The physical target, from the in-repo CC0 ARM scan assets/models/plants/pine_sapling_small/textures/pine_sapling_small_bark_arm_2k.jpg, is AO mean 0.867 with a floor of 0.384 (the deepest fissures occlude 62% of the hemisphere). If art review later demands hue or a true ambient-only AO, that is a SECOND texture and the binding to take is 16.

BRANCH FORKS HAVE A COLLAR, NOT A FLANGE (FENCED FOLLOW-UP, not the v0.1089 bark rung - do not accept a bark normal map as a fix for it, the silhouette is the cue). On the nearest fork the limb must SWELL where it meets its parent (base radius >= 1.25x the limb's radius one limb-diameter out) and no fork may show a flat straight-edged plate longer than 8 px where two tubes clip. Photographed at v0.1088.2 in .probe-rig-bark2/closeups/p11.png: limb and trunk interpenetrate as clean cylinders leaving a hard-edged quadrilateral flange. Real attachment grows a branch collar (a swollen annular ring of trunk tissue wrapping the branch base) plus a raised bark ridge out of the crotch. GEOMETRY work in tree_mesh.rs limb()/welded_root(): one extra flared vertex ring per limb (r0 * ~1.35 tapering to r0 over ~1.5 * r0).

CARD SHADOWS ARE TREE-SHAPED: no rectangular dark patch on open ground with no visible tree. MEASURED v0.1105.1: both shadow pipelines were `fragment: None` (pipeline.rs:564, :709), so a 21 m card cast a solid 21 m board. The geometry: a card is sized `s = frame_m * h / h_nominal` (fir frame 23.1 m, nominal 22.0 m), so a 20 m fir is a 21x21 m quad whose baked sprite is only about 15-25% opaque inside that frame - the caster was 4-7x the true silhouette and threw a solid rectangle roughly 36 m downsun at a 30 degree sun. Operator report: "we would get weird chunks that would not spawn trees visually but they were still affecting the light. As I would move around the chunk that is unloaded would change" - the moving half of that is the LOD crossfade dither, which discarded in colour and not in shadow, so a patch fading OUT kept casting at full strength until the swap finished. WHAT TO LOOK FOR: walk a straight line across open ground beside a stand and watch the shade. Every shadow edge must follow a crown outline; no shaded rectangle may sit where no tree stands, and none may appear or vanish as a patch changes LOD. This is the same failure the CANOPY CASTS DAPPLE gate predicted in its straight-edge half - read them together. FIXED v0.1106 by `fs_shadow` in assets/shaders/pbr/90-fragment-main.wgsl, which mirrors four fs_main discards (LOD dither, type 19 photoscan alpha < 0.35, type 21 cluster card alpha < 0.5, type 12 sprite-atlas alpha < 0.5) and deliberately omits the two eye-distance card gates. The classic path SPLITS - "Sun Shadow Pipeline" stays depth-only for opaque casters, "Sun Shadow Alpha Pipeline" carries the fragment stage - while the patch path always carries it, because a chunk ground and its cards share one index range. CI twin: renderer::pipeline::shadow_cutout_tests fails if a threshold changes on one side only. STILL OPEN AT v0.1106, do not read this gate as fully closed: the type 19 / type 21 branches of fs_shadow sample the per-material albedo at group(3) binding 0, and the shadow pass binds the 1x1 WHITE fallback there (the per-material group 3 also carries the real shadow map at binding 6, which wgpu will not let a pass sample while writing it). Alpha 1 means those two never discard yet, so NEAR-TREE foliage quads still stamp their full rectangle. Closing it needs a shadow-safe per-material group 3 (same entries, dummy depth at binding 6) bound per draw in the classic caster loop.

vantages.desc: Standing in the Fuji forest looking DOWN at the ground 1-6 m ahead - the distance at which grass is actually judged
vantages._why: Both existing fuji vantages aim within 10 deg of the horizon, so the near-field ground has never had rig coverage. Added v0.1090 with the instanced grass-strand layer, which replaced the baked grass cards outright. The layer it replaced was measured at 0.087 tufts/m2 (one per 11.5 m2) for an effective LAI of 0.033 against a real turf canopy's 1.9-6.0, and at THIS site it emitted nothing at all: its gate was patch depth >= 18 and the LOD selector never got past 16 here.

vantages.expect: A continuous grass sward filling the frame: individual blades readable at 1-3 m, ARCHING rather than spiky, litter/soil visible only through gaps between clumps. The ground is never a smooth plane. The sward is CLUMPED - visibly thicker and thinner patches with occasional bare scrapes, not a uniform mat. Blade colour belongs to the ground it grows in (this is conifer-duff Fuji, not lawn), with a minority of dry yellowed tissue, and each blade is darker at its base than at its tip.
regressions: GROUND IS NOT A PAINTED PLANE. In box (60,150)-(1210,630) at 1280x720, scaled proportionally at other widths, the fraction of 16x16 px blocks whose internal luma SD is below 3/255 must be under 10%, and high-pass luma SD (subtract a 33x33 box mean) divided by mean luma must be at least 0.30. Deliberately COLOUR-AGNOSTIC so it survives the grass tint tracking the ground. MEASURED v0.1088.4 at 1280x720 on the layer this replaced: 99.8% flat blocks / 0.111 at look_offset 25 and 99.0% / 0.106 at 45 - the ground was mathematically flat at block scale. NO BASELINE HAS BEEN TAKEN ON THE NEW BUILD: the grass-strands increment (v0.1090) shipped the CPU layer and its CI twins but the GPU draw is a pending wiring step, so nothing here has been through the rig yet. Baseline AT 2560 on the first build that draws the layer, and do NOT paste any number from the v0.1085 fidelity pass into this file - every one of those was measured on a frame that contained no grass at all (66 of 71 ChunkDiag lines at dmax=17, hist[18]=0, alt 1238 m) and on blobs that were foliage blades, not tufts.

GRASS MOVES IN WIND. vantages.desc: Inside the cloud layer at 3 km, heavy cover, looking level - the operator's ascent condition where the shelf that follows the camera appears.
vantages.expect: No hard horizontal line. Cloud detail must not change abruptly along one screen row.
vantages._why: Operator screenshots at 5.7 and 6.2 km show a hard horizontal line with smoother cloud above and sharper, grainier cloud below. It is the cloud BASE-shell tangent. Inside the slab m0 is 0 for every ray and only m1 varies, and m1 is clipped where a ray dives below the base - so the marched segment steps 245 to 619 km across that tangent, a factor of 2.530 (log2 = 1.339). The tangent sits 2.201 degrees below horizontal at 5.7 km and 2.315 at 6.2 km, which is exactly where the line was photographed.
vantages._pair_note: Two altitudes because the line MOVES with altitude (2.20 vs 2.31 degrees). A fix that merely hides it at one altitude will show at the other.
regressions: cloud detail must be continuous across the base-shell horizon
vantages._channel_note: The channel is NOT the segment-relative step law - step_near picks slab_h * 0.045 = 495 m on BOTH sides for the first ~109 km of every ray, so the step is identical across the line. It is the per-ray frozen footprint g_v2_foot_m, taken at the segment MIDPOINT, which inherits the same 2.530x jump and sets the density rind AND four shape mips (displacement, second displacement, domain warp, interior turbulence). That is 1.34 mip levels of surface detail changing along one screen row.
vantages._gate_note: The first cut of these vantages pinned neither cloud_type nor enough cover, so the seam row held no cloud and the metric scored empty sky against empty sky. cloud_type 0.46 gives convective towers that reach above the camera, putting cloud on BOTH sides of the tangent; cloud_cover 0.85 fills the deck below so the GROUND horizon is hidden. That last part matters: the base tangent and the ground horizon are only about 3 rows apart at these altitudes, so an unfilled deck makes them impossible to tell apart. Cover retuned 0.85 -> 0.55 after the sheet union (v0.1234): 0.85 became a genuinely closed deck and the camera sat inside featureless cloud, scoring empty again. The shelf lives among distinct clouds.

vantages.desc: The same close cumulus camera at near-full coverage. Tests whether the field can actually CLOSE UP.
vantages.expect: A filled deck. Gaps between clouds should be the exception, not the rule.
vantages._why: Operator: "a place that looks like it is supposed to have big dense clouds are instead rendering as smaller than their container... the cloud chunks can never get large enough to fill the presently empty space." The occupancy law sets p = coverage * cell_area / cloud_area and CLAMPS it at 1, so once every cell holds its one cloud the field saturates at whatever a single cloud fills - measured ceilings 17.7% (humilis), 30.2% (congestus), 52.2% (stratocumulus). Any requested coverage above those was unreachable. This vantage asks for far more than the ceiling, which is the only place the defect is visible.
vantages._pair_note: Runs with cumulus-closeup-high. High uses the noise body, Ultra the constructed one; the pair is what tells apart "the bodies improved" from "the whole sky changed".
regressions: constructed cloud bodies must not read as spheres

vantages.desc: Straight down on the deck at near-full coverage. The only view where screen coverage EQUALS areal coverage.
vantages.expect: A filled deck at cloud_cover 0.95. Large gaps mean the field cannot reach the coverage it was asked for.
vantages._why: The occupancy law controls AREAL coverage, so it must be measured from nadir. regressions: the cloud field must reach the coverage the weather asks for
